verses.text: The whole community of Israel gathered at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting there. The land was now under their control.
But seven tribes of Israel had still not received their share of land.
So Joshua said to the Israelites, "How long will you wait before you go and take the land the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you?
Choose three men from each tribe. I will send them out to travel through the land and write a description of it, showing how it can be shared. Then they will come back to me.
They are to divide the land into seven parts. Judah will stay in its land in the south, and Joseph's descendants in their land in the north.
Write descriptions of the seven parts and bring them here to me. Then I will draw lots for you here in the presence of the LORD our God.

The Levites, however, get no share among you, because serving as priests of the LORD is their share. And Gad, Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their land east of the Jordan, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them."
As the men set out, Joshua told them, "Go through the land and write a description of it. Then come back to me, and I will draw lots for you here at Shiloh before the LORD."
So the men went through the land and wrote a description of it in a book, town by town, in seven parts. Then they came back to Joshua in the camp at Shiloh.
Joshua drew lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD, and there he shared out the land to the Israelites, tribe by tribe.
The first lot came out for the tribe of Benjamin, clan by clan. Their land lay between the land of Judah and the land of Joseph.
On the north side their border began at the Jordan, ran along the northern slope of Jericho, and went west into the hill country, coming out at the desert of Beth Aven.
From there it crossed to the southern slope of Luz, which is Bethel, and went down to Ataroth Addar, on the hill south of Lower Beth Horon.

From the hill facing Beth Horon on the south, the border turned south along the western side and ended at Kiriath Baal, which is Kiriath Jearim, a town of the people of Judah. This was the western side.
The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath Jearim on the west and went to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

The border went down to the foot of the hill facing the Valley of Ben Hinnom, at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim. It went down the Hinnom Valley along the southern slope of the Jebusite city, and on down to En Rogel.
Then it curved north, went to En Shemesh, continued to Geliloth, which faces the Pass of Adummim, and went down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
It went on to the northern slope facing the Jordan valley and down into the valley.
Then it went to the northern slope of Beth Hoglah and ended at the northern bay of the Dead Sea, where the Jordan flows in. This was the southern border.
The Jordan formed the border on the east side. These were the borders all around the land given to the clans of Benjamin.
The tribe of Benjamin, clan by clan, had these towns: Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz,
Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,
Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,
Kephar Ammoni, Ophni and Geba. There were twelve towns and their villages.
Then Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,
Mizpah, Kephirah, Mozah,
Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,
Zelah, Haeleph, the Jebusite city, which is Jerusalem, Gibeah and Kiriath. There were fourteen towns and their villages. This was the land given to the clans of Benjamin.
